Benson County sits in north central North Dakota. Minnewaukan is the county seat. This guide explains how Benson County tax deed sales work, where to check sale updates, and what investors should know before bidding. North Dakota does not sell private tax lien certificates the way many other states do. It sells county held tax deed property after the tax foreclosure process ends.

What Is Benson County Tax Deed Investing?

Benson County tax deed investing means buying property that the county took after unpaid property taxes were not cured. State law says the county may sell land acquired by tax deed at public auction. This is not an interest paying lien certificate sale. Buyers bid for the property itself.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • Benson County tax deed investing involves purchasing properties after unpaid taxes, with the sale occurring at public auction.
  • The annual tax deed sale is set for the third Tuesday of November, and property details will be posted ahead of time.
  • Investors benefit from lower property values and potential high returns, provided they conduct thorough due diligence.
  • The auction process includes minimum bids and cash or installment payments, leading to deed transfer after full payment.
  • Benson County offers unique economic advantages for investors, including a low-density population and recreational opportunities.

North Dakota law sets the annual tax deed sale for the third Tuesday of November. The sale must happen at the county auditor office or the usual district court place. The county must post notice at the auditor office at least 15 days before sale. It must also publish notice in the county newspaper at least 10 days before sale.

Fun Facts About Benson County

  • Benson County has about 5,700 residents.
  • The county has about 1,388 square miles of land.
  • Median owner occupied home value is about $90,000.
  • The Benson County courthouse has deep local history and was built after county voters backed a bond issue for a permanent courthouse.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions: Devils Lake area, local parks, hunting, fishing, and historic county sites.
  • Transportation: US and state routes connect Minnewaukan, Maddock, Leeds, and nearby towns.
  • Economy: Farming, local services, public work, small business, and outdoor travel.
  • Community: Benson County promotes year round activities and outdoor life. Maddock highlights parks, hunting, fishing, farming, and swimming.

Why Benson County Is Ideal for Tax Deed Investors

  • Lower home values may create low entry points.
  • Tax deed sales can offer high returns when buyers research well.
  • This can be a low risk investment only when title, access, and repairs are checked.
  • North Dakota gives state tax lien opportunities through a tax deed path.
  • Buyers compete for real property, not just paper liens.

Auction Process for Benson County Tax Deed Sales

The Benson County tax deed sale follows North Dakota law. The county first takes tax deed title after proper notice and an uncured tax lien. Then the county appraises the property before the annual sale. The minimum price should cover taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest, costs, and current estimated taxes when value allows.

How the Auction Works

  1. Step 1: Notice is posted and published

    The county posts sale notice at the Auditor office. It also publishes notice in the official county newspaper. This notice should list the parcel, address when available, and minimum sale price.

  2. Step 2: Buyers check each property

    Review the tax record, property card, maps, access, liens, and repair needs. Do not bid only because the opening price looks low.

  3. Step 3: Bidding starts at the minimum price

    Each parcel sells to the highest qualified bidder. State law says a bidder is not qualified if that person owes delinquent taxes to any North Dakota county.

  4. Step 4: Payment follows county terms

    The sale may be cash. It may also allow one fourth down with the balance paid in yearly installments for up to 10 years. The county board sets any contract interest rate. It cannot exceed 12 percent.

  5. Step 5: Buyer receives county deed after payment

    After full payment, the county auditor gives a deed for the county interest in the property. The property becomes taxable to the buyer once the deed or contract is delivered.

Maximum Returns and Expected Returns on Benson County Tax Deed Property

Benson County tax deed buyers do not earn a fixed lien interest rate. The return comes from equity, resale, rent, land use, or long term hold value. Expected returns depend on bid price, title condition, access, cleanup, repairs, and demand.

Maximum returns can be high when a buyer wins far below market value and the property has clean title and usable access. Returns can also shrink fast if the parcel has bad access, code issues, occupants, or repair costs.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

North Dakota law does not show a citizenship limit in the tax deed sale rules reviewed. It does say a person cannot be the highest bidder if that person owes delinquent taxes to any county in North Dakota. Foreign buyers should confirm payment rules, tax forms, deed recording needs, and legal service rules before bidding.

Importance of Due Diligence in Benson County Tax Deed Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check the property tax record.
  • Review the legal description.
  • Study maps and road access.
  • Order a title search.
  • Check special assessments.
  • Inspect from public roads only.
  • Ask about occupants and debris.
  • Call the Auditor before bidding.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • You may buy land with no legal access.
  • A building may need major repairs.
  • Occupants may delay your plan.
  • Title issues may slow resale.
  • Special assessments may affect your cost.
  • A low bid can still become a bad buy.

Buying OTC Tax Deeds in Benson County

How to Purchase OTC Tax Deeds

North Dakota law allows property not sold at the annual November sale to be sold by the county auditor before the next annual sale. The price cannot be less than the minimum sale price unless the board reappraises and approves a new value. Contact the Benson County Auditor for any unsold tax deed property list.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

OTC buying may mean less bidding pressure. It may also give you more time to study the parcel. You still need strong research. The same title, access, repair, and resale questions matter.

Why Benson County Is a Top Choice for Tax Deed Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Benson County has a small population and a low density.
  • Lower housing values may create room for value buys.
  • Farming, outdoor use, and small town housing shape demand.
  • Devils Lake and local recreation can help certain land types.
  • North Dakota law gives a clear tax deed sale process.

Real Estate Market Overview

Benson County is a rural market. That can help patient buyers. It can also slow resale. Investors should focus on usable lots, homes with clear access, farm related land, and parcels near services. According to our review, the best deals are usually the ones with simple access, clear use, and repair costs you can prove before bidding.

Conclusion

Benson County, North Dakota tax deed sales can be a smart way to study low cost property. The sale is not a tax lien certificate sale. Buyers bid on county held tax deed property. The annual sale starts on the third Tuesday of November under state law. The county notice gives the exact sale terms.

Do thorough research before bidding. Check title, access, condition, special assessments, and resale demand. Smart investing starts before the auction.

Pro Tips

  • Call Bonnie Erickson before November and ask how the next sale will run.
  • Watch the county notice board and official newspaper before the sale.
  • Use the county tax search to study unpaid taxes and parcel data.
  • Favor parcels near roads, towns, lake areas, or clear farm use.
  • Do not assume a cheap parcel is a good deal.

FAQs About Benson County Tax Deeds

Can I sell right after I win?

Maybe, but title work may be needed first.

Do I need quiet title?

Ask a North Dakota real estate attorney before resale.

Do other liens survive?

Some interests may matter. Always order a title search.

Can I enter the property after winning?

Wait until you have legal rights and local advice.

Can I finance a tax deed buy?

Most buyers use cash. Lenders may want title cleanup first.
